description:
FILED s543m (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24): the RESIDUE of #5354 that s543m did not take (s543m took the container clears `%h = ()` / `@a = ()` / `undef %h` / `undef @a` and the void `pop` / `shift` / `splice`).  PRE-EXISTING.

REPRODUCERS (perl 5.40.3 prints 5 | PCL 0; scratch/s543m/p7/m7.pl rows x y):
    my $f = "/tmp/x.$$"; my %h; { open my $t, ">", $f or die; print $t "hdata"; $h{fh} = $t; } $h{fh} = undef; print -s $f, "\n";
    (and `$a[0] = undef;`, `$r->{fh} = undef;`)
    my $f = "/tmp/x.$$"; my %h; { open my $t, ">", $f or die; print $t "hdata"; $h{fh} = $t; } sub drop { delete $h{fh} } drop(); print -s $f, "\n";

WHY NOT TAKEN (s543m's measurement, a line-regex census of the 2,047-file wide list, scratch/s543m/tools/dropcount.pl): `$h{K} = undef;` statements 135 in 38 files; a block-tail `delete ...}` 106 in 75 files.
  * ELEMENT = undef: the flush must read the OLD element before the store without a FETCH (a tied hash's STORE alone is what perl runs) and without vivifying -- a runtime peek of the raw table / vector slot (the delete wrap reads delete's own value; there is no such value here).  Design: a statement shape in Pl::Stmt (the element place + a literal undef right side) and a runtime `%p-flush-dropped-elem CONTAINER KEY` that peeks the slot as %p-flush-dropped-value does (no tie, +p-flush-walk-limit+).
  * SUB TAIL `delete`: the statement is lowered `inherit` (its value is the sub's return); the wrap (p-flush-dropped-value FORM) returns FORM's value unchanged, but it would change the emission of every sub ending in `delete $self->{k}` (75 files of the census) for a rare drop -- the brief's cost rule: measure the wide A/B and the bench first.

=== DONE (s543m, Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24; taken after the USER's ORDINARY-or-RARE ruling) ===
ELEMENT = undef: `$h{K} = undef;` / `$r->{K} = undef;` / `$a[I] = undef;` / `$r->[I] = undef;` (Pl::Stmt::drop_store_shape: the one-level element of the delete arm, `=`, the word `undef`) -- as a statement or a sub's tail (`sub close_it { $_[0]{fh} = undef }`).  The lowered store `(setf (p-gethash|p-aref C K) V)` / `(p-setf (p-gethash-deref|p-aref-deref C K) V)` with C a variable (Parser2::_drop_store_form_p) is wrapped `(p-flush-dropped-store FORM)`: the macro binds K once, %p-flush-dropped-elem PEEKS the raw slot (a tied container skipped: one STORE, no FETCH -- probed; nothing vivified: `$u->{k} = undef` still makes $u a HASH ref) and flushes it as p-flush-dropped-value does, then the store runs.
SUB TAIL: a TAIL `delete` / `pop` / `shift` (lowered `inherit`, outside eval text) takes `(p-flush-dropped-value FORM :tail)`: flushed only when the caller's context is VOID -- `$o->drop;` drops the handle (perl writes its bytes), `my $fh = $o->take_fh` keeps it (perl does NOT write them: probed 0 bytes; the first cut flushed there and was wrong).  The tail's value is unchanged.
PROBES: scratch/s543m/p7/m7.pl rows x y + p7/m7b.pl 13 lines: base 5 of 15 (the value controls), tree 15 of 15.
GUARD: Pl/t/fh-collect-01.t row 14 (FAILS on the base).  Commit 94b5a6a9 (WIP 9).  Costs: the session log's bench rows (`hundef`, `taildel`).
frequency_reason: an output handle dropped by `$self->{fh} = undef` or a sub-tail delete: the ordinary way an object lets go of its handle (first pass from the subject, the reviewing session 2026-11-24)
subject: SILENT WRONG: an element overwritten with undef (`$h{fh} = undef;`, `$a[0] = undef;`) and a sub-TAIL `delete $h{fh}` drop an escaped output handle without writing it out (the residue of #5354 s543m did not take)
triage_reason: the residue of #5354 (a live silent wrong of the drop flush): IN
